payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image’s content read as a drawing rather than a photograph with blur, grain, or texture overlaid?
node.criteria: pass: evidence identifies drawn or illustrated rendering replacing photographic detail across the image’s content, including prominent subjects and surrounding areas; fail: evidence identifies retained photographic rendering with only blur, grain, or texture overlays; unknown: visible cues do not reliably distinguish drawing conversion from filtered photography. State the specific cues supporting the judgment and note any substantial photographic areas.
node.binding: Assess drawing-form conversion and its extent across the image. Do not assess chalk medium; do not treat sketch-like outlines, blur, or texture alone as proof of conversion.

node_traces.evidence: The giraffes and their spots retain photographic detail and realistic shading, while the trees, ground, and sky show strong directional blur and grain-like texture. These overlays do not replace the photographic rendering with drawn or illustrated forms across the image.

The giraffes and landscape retain photographic detail and shading, with recognizable natural textures and lighting. A strong grainy, smudged effect and sketch-like outlines are overlaid, but the image does not read as a drawing replacing photographic rendering across its content.

The giraffes retain realistic photographic anatomy, coat patterns, and shading, while the trees, ground, and background are mainly softened and streaked with a texture overlay. The image does not show a drawn or illustrated rendering replacing photographic detail across its content.

The giraffes and landscape retain photographic detail and shading, with recognizable natural textures and lighting. A strong grainy, smudged effect and sketch-like outlines are overlaid, but the image does not read as a drawing replacing photographic rendering across its content.

The giraffes and background retain photographic detail and shading, with their original forms and textures still visible. A strong blur/grain-like overlay and sketchy outlines are present, but the image does not read as a drawing replacing photographic rendering across its content.

n3: The binding is too underspecified for a stable decision: it names the target and chalk drawing but does not expose the node’s three-way aggregation rule. Make the typed criteria explicit: complete only when saved evidence supports both chalk medium and drawing conversion across the image; partial when either requested aspect is affirmatively present but completion is not established; absent only when evidence affirmatively shows no requested progress; unknown when evidence is insufficient. Do not let a fail/unknown on one aspect erase positive evidence for the other, and do not treat a dependency or transport failure as visual evidence. The traces vary between unknown and partial because chalk-like texture is sometimes indistinguishable from generic filtering, while repeated observations also report photographic giraffe detail beneath blur/grain overlays. Preserve that distinction: those observations support partial when chalk treatment is affirmatively established, not complete conversion. Keep the node restricted to saved observations and avoid adding visual requirements beyond the instruction.
